questions.question: What are the default capacity and load factor of a new HashMap?
questions.explanation: new HashMap<>() starts with 16 buckets and resizes when it becomes 75% full.

questions.question: Since Java 8, when does a HashMap bucket change from a linked list to a red-black tree?
options: As soon as a second key collides
When one bucket reaches 8 nodes and the table has at least 64 buckets
Never; buckets are always linked lists
questions.explanation: TREEIFY_THRESHOLD is 8. If the table is smaller than 64 buckets, HashMap resizes instead of building a tree.

questions.question: What does this print? Map<String, Integer> m = new HashMap<>(); m.put("A", 1); System.out.println(m.put("A", 5));
questions.explanation: put returns the previous value for the key. The key A held 1 before it was replaced by 5.

questions.question: What does this print? Map<String, Integer> m = new HashMap<>(); m.put(null, 3); m.put(null, 9); System.out.println(m.get(null) + " " + m.size());
questions.explanation: HashMap allows one null key. The second put replaces 3 with 9, so there is still only one entry.

questions.question: A Seat class overrides equals() but not hashCode(). After map.put(new Seat("C1", 4), "Ravi"), why does map.get(new Seat("C1", 4)) return null?
options: HashMap cannot store custom objects as keys
equals() is never called by HashMap
The key must be a String
The two equal seats get different default hash codes, so get looks in the wrong bucket
questions.explanation: Equal objects must have equal hash codes. Without hashCode(), Object's version gives each instance its own code.

questions.question: How does HashMap turn a spread hash into a bucket index for a table of size n?
questions.explanation: n is always a power of two, so masking with n - 1 gives the same result as a positive modulo, but faster.

questions.question: A HashMap has 16 buckets and load factor 0.75. Which put causes the first resize?
questions.explanation: The threshold is 16 x 0.75 = 12. The table doubles when the size goes past 12, which happens on the 13th entry.

questions.question: What does this print? Map<String, Integer> m = new HashMap<>(); System.out.println(m.getOrDefault("Z", 0) + 1);
questions.explanation: Z is missing, so getOrDefault returns the fallback 0, and 0 + 1 is 1.

questions.question: Why does this line fail at run time? Map<String, String> t = new Hashtable<>(); t.put(null, "x");
options: Hashtable does not allow null keys and throws NullPointerException
Map cannot point to a Hashtable
questions.explanation: Hashtable rejects null keys and null values. HashMap allows one null key and many null values.

questions.question: You need a map whose keys always come out in sorted order. Which class fits best?
questions.explanation: TreeMap keeps keys in a red-black tree ordered by compareTo or a Comparator. LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order.
